questions.question: What picture of the universe is given at the beginning of this passage?
questions.answer: It is described like a well-run kingdom or city where everything has its own job and follows order.

questions.question: What are all things and living groups shown doing in that kingdom-like universe?
questions.answer: They are carrying out their duties in an obedient and orderly way.

questions.question: What does the mention of the armies of the heavens and the earth help show?
questions.answer: It helps show that Allah has complete rule and authority over everything.

questions.question: Which levels are included in these “armies” in the passage?
questions.answer: They include very tiny things, plants, animals, and even the stars.

questions.question: What main truth is being explained in this section?
questions.answer: The section explains the truth of absolute sovereignty.

questions.question: Why does the passage say partners cannot be joined with Allah in His rule?
questions.answer: Because true and complete rule does not allow shared control.

questions.question: What would happen if many strong hands tried to run the same work at once?
questions.answer: The result would be disorder and confusion.

questions.question: What example is given from human leadership to explain this point?
questions.answer: The passage says that if two rulers were over one land, order would break down.

questions.question: Instead of confusion, what do we actually see in creation?
questions.answer: We see order everywhere.

questions.question: What are two examples the passage gives to show order in both small and large things?
questions.answer: It gives examples from a fly’s wing and from the heavenly lights.

questions.question: What other two examples show order inside living things and in space?
questions.answer: It mentions body cells and the signs or movements of the planets.

questions.question: What does this complete order prove about Allah’s rule?
questions.answer: It proves that no partner is taking part in His management.

questions.question: Why would accepting a rival go against sovereignty itself?
questions.answer: Because sovereignty has honor and dignity, and sharing it with a rival would go against that honor.

questions.question: What human example is used to show how strongly rule rejects rivals?
questions.answer: It says even weak human beings may fight very cruelly for small and temporary power.

questions.question: If weak people guard tiny power so fiercely, what does the passage lead us to understand about Allah?
questions.answer: It leads us to understand that Allah, who has absolute power and owns all creation, would never allow any partner in His sacred rule.

questions.question: What comparison is used to help us understand the universe in this passage?
questions.answer: The universe is compared to a successful kingdom and a wisely governed city.

questions.question: How are the things in the universe described within that comparison?
questions.answer: They are described as obedient workers or members of an organized system.

questions.question: What does the word “sovereignty” mean here in a simple way?
questions.answer: It means complete rule, command, and authority.

questions.question: How does the passage use the idea of armies to teach about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It shows that all parts of creation are like organized forces under one command.

questions.question: Does the passage limit these armies to only one part of creation or many parts?
questions.answer: It includes many parts of creation, from the smallest things to the stars.

questions.question: What does such wide-reaching order point to?
questions.answer: It points to Allah’s total authority over all creation.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is false about giving partners to Allah?
questions.answer: It is false because shared rule would ruin the perfect order we see.

questions.question: What usually happens when several people push to control the same job?
questions.answer: The work becomes mixed up and disorderly.

questions.question: What happens to a country or district when two rulers try to lead it at the same time?
questions.answer: Its order disappears and chaos takes its place.

questions.question: What does the passage say we actually find from tiny creatures to the sky?
questions.answer: We find a steady and amazing order everywhere.

questions.question: Why is the example of a fly important in this passage?
questions.answer: It shows that even the smallest parts of creation are orderly.

questions.question: Why are the stars and planets mentioned too?
questions.answer: They show that this order also reaches the biggest parts of creation.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the relationship between dignity and rule?
questions.answer: It teaches that real rule has dignity and does not accept a competing rival.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention that humans may act brutally for small power?
questions.answer: To show that even weak people dislike sharing power, so Allah’s perfect sovereignty would never be shared.

questions.question: What final conclusion should a student take from this whole section?
questions.answer: Allah alone rules all things, and the order in creation shows that He has no partner.

questions.question: What is the title of the truth explained in the target passage?
questions.answer: It is the truth of sovereignty.

questions.question: How is the cosmos presented to someone who looks carefully at it?
questions.answer: It appears like an active, successful, and wisely managed kingdom.

questions.question: What does the passage say all things and kinds of creatures are doing?
questions.answer: They are obeying and performing their own tasks.

questions.question: Why are commands, laws, and ordered groups mentioned together?
questions.answer: They work together to show planned rule and authority.

questions.question: What range of creation is covered by these ordered groups?
questions.answer: They stretch from atoms and plants to animals and stars.

questions.question: What do these signs clearly prove, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They clearly prove absolute sovereignty and universal authority.

questions.question: What claim does the passage reject after proving absolute sovereignty?
questions.answer: It rejects the idea that Allah could have any partner.

questions.question: What is the effect of many controlling hands entering one task?
questions.answer: The task ends in confusion.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the example of two kings in one land?
questions.answer: One land cannot stay orderly under rival rulers.

questions.question: How does the passage use examples from both nature and the sky?
questions.answer: It uses them to show that order exists in every level of creation.

questions.question: What does order in body cells suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that even hidden and tiny parts are under careful control.

questions.question: What does order in the heavenly bodies suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that the vast universe is also under the same control.

questions.question: Why is there said to be no room for a partner in Allah’s affairs?
questions.answer: Because the perfect order everywhere leaves no sign that anyone else is sharing His work.

questions.question: What quality of sovereignty would be insulted by accepting a rival?
questions.answer: Its dignity and honor would be insulted.

questions.question: What argument is made from human weakness to Allah’s absolute power?
questions.answer: If weak humans fight over small power, then Allah, who has complete power and ownership, would never allow anyone to share His sovereignty.

questions.question: What is one main idea taught by comparing the universe to a kingdom?
questions.answer: The idea is that creation is ruled with wisdom, purpose, and order.

questions.question: In that kingdom-like picture, how do created things behave?
questions.answer: They behave like obedient servants carrying out assigned duties.

questions.question: Why does the passage refer to armies in the heavens and the earth?
questions.answer: To show that all creation is arranged under one command.

questions.question: What small and large parts of creation are included in this ordered system?
questions.answer: Very tiny things, plants, animals, and stars are all included.

questions.question: What two truths do these signs point to?
questions.answer: They point to complete sovereignty and authority over all.

questions.question: Why does complete sovereignty leave no room for partners?
questions.answer: Because real complete rule cannot be divided between equals.

questions.question: What simple everyday principle is used to explain this?
questions.answer: When too many rulers take over the same matter, confusion follows.

questions.question: How does the example of two local leaders help the reader understand the point?
questions.answer: It shows that even in a small area, competing leaders ruin order.

questions.question: What do we see in the world instead of ruined order?
questions.answer: We see careful order everywhere we look.

questions.question: Which examples show this order in both living bodies and outer space?
questions.answer: The passage mentions cells in the body and signs of the planets.

questions.question: What can we infer from order appearing at every level of creation?
questions.answer: We can infer that one supreme ruler is managing all of it.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the dignity of sovereignty?
questions.answer: It says sovereignty has such dignity that it does not accept a rival.

questions.question: Why is the human struggle for small authority mentioned?
questions.answer: It is mentioned as a lower example to help us understand how much more impossible rivalry is in Allah’s sovereignty.

questions.question: What kind of sovereignty do humans fight over in the example?
questions.answer: They fight over a small, passing, and outward kind of power.

questions.question: What is the conclusion about Allah from the end of the passage?
questions.answer: Allah, the Owner of all creation and absolute power, never allows anyone to share in His sacred sovereignty.

questions.question: What does a thoughtful person notice when looking at the universe, according to this passage?
questions.answer: He notices that it is like a thriving kingdom or city run with wisdom and strength.

questions.question: What do all creatures and groups of creatures seem to be doing in that universe?
questions.answer: They seem to be carrying out their own assigned work in obedience.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the rule found throughout creation?
questions.answer: It describes it as complete sovereignty and authority over all things.

questions.question: Why are atoms, plants, animals, and stars all mentioned together?
questions.answer: They show that one system of rule covers everything from the smallest to the greatest.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the truth of assigning partners to Allah?
questions.answer: It says there is no truth in it.

questions.question: What is the first reason given against multiple rulers over one work?
questions.answer: The first reason is that many claimants over one job cause disorder.

questions.question: What human leadership example supports that reason?
questions.answer: The example is that two kings in one country would destroy order.

questions.question: What opposite condition do we actually witness in creation?
questions.answer: We witness harmony and order everywhere.

questions.question: How do the examples in the passage move from tiny things to huge things?
questions.answer: They move from a fly’s wing and body cells to the heavens and planets.

questions.question: What does this wide pattern of order tell us about Allah’s works?
questions.answer: It tells us that His works are not being shared with any partner.

questions.question: Besides order, what other reason is given that sovereignty rejects partners?
questions.answer: Another reason is that sovereignty has dignity and does not accept competition.

questions.question: What does the human example teach about the nature of ruling power?
questions.answer: It teaches that even weak beings cling tightly to power and reject rivals.

questions.question: How is Allah different from the human example?
questions.answer: Allah is not weak or temporary; He has absolute power and ownership over all creation.

questions.question: What can we conclude about Allah’s sacred sovereignty?
questions.answer: It belongs to Him alone and cannot be shared.

questions.question: What big lesson about tawhid does this section support?
questions.answer: It supports that Allah is One in His rule and has no partner.

questions.question: Which “truth” is explained in the marked passage?
questions.answer: The fourth truth, which is sovereignty.

questions.question: What two things is the cosmos compared to at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: It is compared to a prosperous kingdom and a wisely governed city.

questions.question: What does this comparison help the reader understand about creation?
questions.answer: It helps the reader understand that creation is organized and ruled with wisdom.

questions.question: How are all things and species described in their actions?
questions.answer: They are described as obediently doing their special functions.

questions.question: What image from the Qur’an is used to explain this organized rule?
questions.answer: The image of the armies of the heavens and the earth is used.

questions.question: What does that image show about Allah’s authority?
questions.answer: It shows that His authority reaches all levels of creation.

questions.question: Which parts of creation are named to show the full range of this authority?
questions.answer: Atoms, plants, animals, and stars are named.

questions.question: What truth is clearly shown by this universal order?
questions.answer: It clearly shows absolute sovereignty.

questions.question: Why would having more than one ruler spoil things?
questions.answer: Because competing rulers would create confusion and destroy order.

questions.question: What do we see in real creation that goes against the idea of many rulers?
questions.answer: We see perfect order everywhere, not chaos.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the honor of sovereignty?
questions.answer: It says sovereignty has dignity and will not accept a rival.

questions.question: How does the behavior of weak humans help explain this point?
questions.answer: Even weak humans may fight harshly over small power, showing that rule strongly resists sharing.

questions.question: What final understanding about Allah should come from this whole passage?
questions.answer: Allah alone has absolute power, ownership, and sovereignty, so no partner can share His rule.
